title: Affine finite-support representatives for truncated direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a set, and $E_i\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] for $i\in I$. Let $S\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\iota_i:E_i\to S$ exhibit an ambient coproduct. Write $F_q=H^q\circ Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For all integers $a,q$ and all affine opens $U\subseteq Y$, the linear map $\bigoplus_{i\in I}\Gamma(U,F_q(\tau_{\ge a}E_i))\to\Gamma(U,F_q(\tau_{\ge a}S))$, whose restriction to the $i$th summand is $\Gamma(U,F_q(\tau_{\ge a}\iota_i))$, is surjective. Here $\tau_{\ge a}$ is canonical lower truncation for the standard cohomological t-structure.

source.place: Tag 08DZ, bounded-below spectral-sequence paragraph, with Tag 015J

proof.text:
Proof. Choose termwise representatives of the ambient coproduct. Exact sums compute
its cohomology as the sum of the summands' cohomology, and these sums are quasi-coherent.
Exact sums commute with lower truncation, so the truncated family and its coproduct
have the common lower bound a. Over an affine open U of Y, the inverse image is qcqs.
The natural bounded-below hypercohomology spectral sequences have second pages
H^p(f⁻¹U,H^r(τ≥a E)). Cohomology of module sheaves on this qcqs inverse image commutes
with sums. Thus the second-page comparison is bijective. Exact sums commute with the
kernels and images of differentials, so all page comparisons are bijective. In total
degree q there are only the finitely many indices 0 ≤ p ≤ q-a. The finite convergent
filtrations therefore give surjectivity on the abutment: lift a section of the top
nonzero graded piece, subtract its image, and repeat in the next filtration step.
Each lift has finite support; the union of the finitely many supports is finite.
For the second-page terms, cohomology of a quasi-coherent module on the qcqs preimage of an affine open V commutes with localization at a pulled-back section: affine acyclicity and section localization give the affine case, and finite affine covers with quasi-compact overlaps give the general case by Mayer--Vietoris. Compatibility with restriction to principal opens of V and the higher-direct-image presheaf description prove quasi-coherence of the second-page sheaves. Kernel and cokernel closure give quasi-coherence of each later page by induction. Starting at the zero last filtration step, extension closure along the short exact sequences of the finite convergent filtration gives quasi-coherence of the abutment. This derives the required bounded-below quasi-coherence locally inside the spectral-sequence argument; it does not invoke the derived-direct-image bounded-below quasi-coherence theorem, whose imports reach the original truncated-coproduct comparison.
Consequently, exact sections on the affine open U identify the sheaf abutments with
the displayed section modules. Naturality identifies the map with the displayed
linear map. If q<a the target is zero. If I is empty the ambient coproduct and its
lower truncation are zero, so the target is zero as well.

theorem truncated_directImage_affine_finiteSupport
    {X Y : Scheme.{u₁}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (I : Type u₁) (E : I → schemeDerivedQCohCategory X)
    (S : schemeDerivedCategory X) (ι : ∀ i, (E i).obj ⟶ S)
    (hc : IsColimit (Cofan.mk S ι)) (a q : ℤ) (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    Function.Surjective
      (DirectSum.toModule ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op U)) I
        (((SheafOfModules.evaluation (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) (op U)).obj
          ((schemeHigherDirectImage f q).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).obj S))))
        (fun i ↦ ((SheafOfModules.evaluation (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) (op U)).map
          ((schemeHigherDirectImage f q).map
            ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).map (ι i)))).hom))
